To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the hierarchical structure of the ImageNet database allows for an efficient propagation of segmentation, and (ii) the resulting segmentation annotations can be used to train state of the art models for semantic segmentation.
we propose a novel method to automatically annotate ImageNet with pixelwise object segmentations and show that it outperforms the current state of the art in the literature.

(i) a simple propagation strategy can be very effective in automatically annotating large scale databases with segmentations, (ii) the hierarchical structure of the database is an important asset for the propagation, (iii) the propagation can be efficiently implemented on superpixels, and (iv) the method delivers state of the Art results on co-segmentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic propagation of segmentation in a large scale database.
the problem of automatic image segmentation, a fundamental task in computer vision.
automatic annotation of large scale datasets with pixelwise segmentations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to automatically annotate ImageNet with accurate pixelwise object segmentations.
our method is able to automatically annotate a wide range of ImageNet classes with pixelwise object segmentations, and that the results are of high quality and scale to a large number of classes.
we show how to propagate a segmentation to new images and new classes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our method is able to propagate segmentations from one image to another image of the same class.
we propose a scalable and effective technique to automatically annotate ImageNet with pixelwise segmentations, which is the largest dataset of its kind.
we are able to automatically segment a large number of classes, and we do this in a hierarchical way, which allows for the propagation of information between classes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hierarchical structure of large scale databases can be exploited to propagate segmentation annotations efficiently, even without human interaction.
a large scale database of object class segmentations can be efficiently built by propagating segmentation from one class to another.
a large scale database can be populated with pixelwise segmentations by leveraging its own structure.
